title: The Probationary Pledge
logline: Two estranged former crewmates each secretly hire an outsider to pay off the other's punitive sobriety bond, unknowingly liquidating their own livelihoods in a mutual attempt to free each other.

roles.description: Grounded hauler pilot serving mandatory ore-quota detox on a smelter station; weary, ashamed, fiercely loyal.
His former flight engineer running a failing repair slip; crippled hands, refuses to leave the station until the pilot is free.
Enforces debt-probation covenants for the smelter board; rigid, meticulous, pocketing statutory processing surcharges.
The industrial intake dock where grounded debtor pilots haul slag under armed monitoring.
A cramped, oil-soaked workshop in the lower station spine barely making rent.
A scratched naval-grade chronometer engraved with the crew's original freighter registry number.

public_situation: Smelter administrators in {system} post the monthly clearance list for grounded pilots working off court-mandated sobriety covenants.
private_truth: The grounded pilot and his mechanic are each secretly bankrupting themselves to pay off the other's indenture, unaware that paying both triggers a cancellation penalty.

beats.public_change: The smelter board opens mining intake scales for independent ore contributions credited against debtor bonds.

missions.reason: She needs twenty tons of heavy ferrite mined and delivered to the intake scale to credit against the pilot's bond before the monthly auction.
missions.private_fact: She sold her last diagnostic machine to buy the mining rights, leaving her workshop unable to service ships.

beats.public_change: The bailiff posts an eviction notice on the mechanic's repair slip for non-payment of dock utility surcharges.

missions.reason: He asks the pilot to recover his grandfather's flight chronometer from a loan shark's lockbox and deposit it to cover the mechanic's arrears.
missions.private_fact: The chronometer is his last heirloom, and selling it leaves him with nothing to show for thirty years in space.

beats.public_change: The probation office opens its final docket before filing indenture extensions.

missions.reason: He requires sealed clearance scrip and receipt ledgers couriered from the registry vault to certify whose bond is officially discharged first.
missions.private_fact: The bailiff's regulations state that if both parties file cross-indemnity waivers simultaneously, the board confiscates both deposits as administrative fines.

player_choice.prompt: The pilot holds both clearance deposits. Filing both at once triggers the board's confiscation rule. The pilot must choose how to apply the funds.

options.label: Apply the pooled funds entirely to clear the pilot's flight bond
Apply the pooled funds to pay off the mechanic's workshop lease

resolutions.reached_by: The pilot allocates the funds to clear the flight bond.
resolutions.summary: {role:probationary_pilot} receives full flight reinstatement, but {role:veteran_mechanic} loses her workshop lease and signs on as his co-pilot.

consequences.public_summary: A hauler helped two stubborn old grease monkeys pool their pennies to get one pilot back in the cockpit.

resolutions.reached_by: The pilot allocates the funds to clear the workshop debt.
resolutions.summary: {role:veteran_mechanic} retains her slip, and {role:probationary_pilot} agrees to serve his remaining six months of probation working as her shop hand.

consequences.public_summary: A pilot helped pay off a foundry dock lease so two veterans could work out their debts on their own terms.

resolutions.reached_by: Both deposits are seized or the chronometer is lost.
resolutions.summary: {role:probation_bailiff} claims both deposits under the cross-indemnity clause, leaving {role:probationary_pilot} and {role:veteran_mechanic} trapped in extended indentures.

loose_threads.detail: The bailiff's assistant admits forty percent of debtor crew releases are nullified each cycle by the exact same cross-indemnity small print.
The ore intake receipts carry property stamps matching an abandoned corporate freight consortium liquidated nine years ago.

radio_hooks: Smelter board reminds grounded pilots that unworked restitution quotas trigger automatic indenture renewals.
Foundry floor tenants protest rising utility surcharges in lower maintenance sectors of {system}.
Registry archives confirm lowest rate of debtor discharge in five quarters across local refining belts.

voice_direction.probationary_pilot: Tired, humble delivery with dry, self-deprecating phrasing. Becomes intensely defensive only when his engineer's well-being is questioned.
voice_direction.veteran_mechanic: Rasping, stubborn cadence worn down by decades on the foundry floor. Refuses pity with sharp, dismissive profanity.
voice_direction.probation_bailiff: Smug, sing-song administrative clerk drone. Quotes paragraph and subclause numbers from memory with evident relish.
